chunks: Muḥammad ibn Qays narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

The Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام ruled concerning a concubine belonging to a man, who bore a child to her master. Then he married her to his slave. Then her master died and freed her, so she married him, and her child inherited from him. Then her child died, and she inherited her husband, the slave. Then the two came disputing, so he said: 'She is my wife; I will not divorce her.' And she said: 'He is my slave; he has not had intercourse with me.' So she was asked: 'Has he had intercourse with you since he became your slave?' She said: 'No.' He said: 'If he had had intercourse with you since he became your slave, I would have punished you. Go, for he is your slave. He has no authority over you. You may sell him if you wish, keep him enslaved if you wish, and free him if you wish.'

key_terms.سَبِيلٌ: legal authority or claim over her
key_terms.سُرِّيَّةٍ: a concubine or slave-woman owned by a man

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman inherits her husband when he is her slave?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning marriage, slavery, and inheritance after changing ownership status. It establishes that when the woman inherited the slave as her property, he no longer retained spousal authority over her, and the Imam عليه السلام judged according to the legal consequences of ownership.
